Style flextable::flextable object according to APA style

Source: R/tables.R
apa_style.Rd

Style flextable::flextable object according to APA style

Usage

apa_style(
  x,
  font_family = NULL,
  font_size = NULL,
  text_color = "black",
  border_color = "black",
  border_width = 0.5,
  line_spacing = NULL,
  horizontal_padding = 3,
  table_align = "left",
  header_align_vertical = c("top", "middle", "bottom"),
  layout = "autofit",
  table_width = NULL,
  markdown = TRUE,
  markdown_header = markdown,
  markdown_body = markdown,
  no_markdown_columns = NULL,
  no_markdown_columns_header = no_markdown_columns,
  separate_headers = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

a flextable::flextable()

font_family

font family (e.g., "Times New Roman" or "Arial"). If NULL (default), the font set with apa7_defaults(font_family = ) (Times New Roman unless changed).

font_size

font size, in points. If NULL (default), the size set with apa7_defaults(font_size = ) (12 unless changed).

text_color

color of the text: an R color name (e.g., "black", the default) or a hex code (e.g., "#333333")

border_color

color of the rules, in the same forms as text_color

border_width

width of the rules, in points (default: 0.5)

line_spacing

spacing between lines of the header and body (e.g., 2 for double spacing or 1 for single spacing). If NULL (default), the spacing set with apa7_defaults(line_spacing = ) (2 unless changed). Table notes are single-spaced.

horizontal_padding

space to the left and right of each cell's contents, in points (default: 3)

table_align

alignment of the table on the page: "left" (default), "center", or "right"

header_align_vertical

vertical alignment of header text when header cells differ in height: "top" (default), "middle", or "bottom"

layout

"autofit" (default) lets the column widths adjust to the contents in Word; "fixed" keeps the widths as set (see flextable::set_table_properties())

table_width

width of the table, in the same forms in every apa7 function: a proportion from 0 to 1 of the default width (the full width of a portrait page unless changed with apa7_defaults(table_width = )), "page" (or "portrait") for the full width of a portrait page, "landscape" for a landscape page, "column" for one column of a two-column page, or a named number: a proportion of one of these widths (e.g., c(landscape = .8)) or a width in inches, cm, or mm (e.g., c(inches = 5)). With 0, the columns are only as wide as their contents need. If NULL (default), the width set by the code chunk's apa7-width option in Quarto (e.g., #| apa7-width: landscape, or #| apa7-width: {landscape: .8} for a named number) or apa7.width option in R Markdown, or "page" for a chunk with apaquarto's apa-twocolumn: true; otherwise, the table_width set with apa7_defaults() (1 unless changed). The widths of the pages and the column are set with the page_width, landscape_width, and column_width arguments of apa7_defaults(). A number greater than 1 is read as inches, with a warning to write it as c(inches = ).

markdown

if TRUE (default), text in the header and body is converted from markdown (e.g., *p* becomes an italic p)

markdown_header, markdown_body

whether the header or the body is converted from markdown (both default to markdown)

no_markdown_columns

body columns whose text is shown as it is, not converted from markdown (unquoted or quoted names, or tidyselect helpers)

no_markdown_columns_header

column headers that are not converted from markdown. By default, the same columns as no_markdown_columns.

separate_headers

if TRUE (default) and the table has one header row, column names with an underscore are split into a column spanner and a header (e.g., Model 1_B becomes "B" under a "Model 1" spanner)

Value

flextable::flextable

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 4:6)
flextable::flextable(d) |>
  apa_style()

x
y
1
4
2
5
3
6
